title: Make the Quirk identity stack and repository topology independently reconstructable
desired_change: Define the canonical distinctions and dependency direction among Quirk Core, Quirk OS, Quirk Systems, and Quirkverse; declare why Quirk Core infrastructure lives in the quirk-os repository; map repository responsibilities, dependency direction, extraction criteria, and non-goals.
expected_outcome: An outsider can locate each concept, explain which layer owns which authority, and predict where a new object belongs without asking Bryan.

risk.rights_or_safety_impact: Ambiguous ownership can cause authoritative definitions to be written into the wrong layer and later treated as canon.

hidden_context_dependencies: The pack calls Quirk Core the owner while the repository is named quirk-os.
The durable identity stack Core → OS → Systems → Quirkverse exists outside this PR but is not defined inside it.
Repository dependency direction and extraction criteria are oral tradition.
Quirk Control is described as an inspection surface but its relation to Quirk OS is not canonicalized here.
acceptance_checks: A new contributor correctly places five representative objects with no oral guidance.
Every primary layer has owner, inputs, outputs, prohibited responsibilities, dependency direction, and extraction criteria.
All references to Core, OS, Systems, Quirkverse, and Control resolve to canonical IDs.
